I'll bring that same commitment to the SMUHSD Board." About me Meet Diana For 18 years, I've taught in public elementary and middle schools including Meadow Heights Elementary School in San Mateo and Bowditch Middle School in Foster City. That experience has taught me how schools and districts really run, and given me a deep appreciation for the diversity that makes our schools strong. I'm also an active parent in our schools. This is my 10th year serving on PTA Executive boards at Meadow Heights Elementary and Abbott Middle School, including four years as PTA president, where I've advocated for students while listening closely to the needs of teachers and families. And I'm your neighbor. I grew up in Burlingame and have called San Mateo home since 2013. I help run several online community groups in our area, including Buy Nothing San Mateo Beresford/Laurelwood, and Meadow Heights Community because I love building connection and supporting the people around me. I'm also a Cub Scout Den Leader for Pack 27, teaching kids early what it means to give back and be active, contributing members of their community. Why am I running? Because I care deeply about this community — and because my experience has prepared me to serve it well. As a teacher in elementary and middle school classrooms, I've worked closely with administration and seen firsthand what students carry with them as they arrive at high school. As a PTA leader, I've made tough calls about funding the programs that support learning. And as a parent with a child at Hillsdale High School, I'm living the high school experience right now, advocating for my own children, and others, navigating our schools. Together, that gives me a full view of what our students and families need, from the classrooms where they're shaped to the hallways where they're preparing for what's next. High school decisions don't start there, they're the culmination of everything before, and I've spent my career in that "before." I've spent years committed to supporting education in our community. https://ginaforbelmont.org.title: Gina Latimerlo Belmont City Council
https://ginaforbelmont.org.text: Gina Latimerlo Belmont City Council 0 Skip to Content 2026 Election Districts/Voting Newsette 2026 For Residents For Businesses Day in the Life Contact & Zoom Hours Open Menu Close Menu 2026 Election Districts/Voting Newsette 2026 For Residents For Businesses Day in the Life Contact & Zoom Hours Open Menu Close Menu 2026 Election Districts/Voting Newsette 2026 For Residents For Businesses Day in the Life Contact & Zoom Hours Resident & Business Owner for 30 years I've been a homeowner, a renter, a college student, a single adult, a community leader, a community activist, a small business owner, a volunteer, a public school parent, a private school parent, a pet owner, a non-pet owner, a wife, a mom, a Councilmember, a Planning Commissioner, a Boardmember, and a Vice Mayor — all in Belmont! Moving into the apartments on Carlmont after graduating from our local university, my husband and I began investing in our community through our activism in the Lions Club. Once we moved into our home in Homeview, I became the President of our Neighborhood Association and began learning how city processes worked. After ten years, I became a Planning Commissioner, and now I’m in the City Council and serving Belmont on a number of County of San Mateo Boards. Through my students volunteering at the annual Save the Music Festival, I was able to integrate my community service life with my small business. The Latimerlo Studio (latimerlo.com) has been training students to sing since 1998 here in Belmont, and my singers have been both adolescent students from every school here, as well as amazing adults from lots of different walks of life. By continuing to listen to the voices throughout our community and referencing my own experiences here in Belmont over the past 25 years — and by engaging in creative problem solving — I'm helping our community figure out ways to use our land, property, spaces, and processes to better the life experiences of everyone in our fantastic community by the bay. Contact me at glatimerlo@belmont.gov to share your ideas and opinions! Priorities 1. Staying ahead of the curve in development projects: Belmont is in a time of growth and transition. District 1 is the both the center of growth and the heart of the commercial and residential communities in Belmont. Let’s make sure we have a true revitalization that works for both the current and future populations of Belmont. 2. Creating pipelines to leadership for leaders of diverse backgrounds: I’ve spent my life empowering voices, and I intend to continue that tradition with special attention to the voices that are often unheard. This includes increasing voter turnout, as well as creating new opportunities for leadership. 3. Accessibility to city government: Including improving communication between residents and city government, encouraging true two-way engagement, making sure all voices are heard, and becoming more responsive to residents through a village approach. 4. Keep Belmont’s Open Space open to everyone: Sharing the land and open space has been the lesson of the last couple of centuries. It’s important to ensure that everyone has equal access to our greenest resources. 5. Continuing to focus on improving infrastructure with our roads, sewers, and storm drains: Our infrastructure sat idly degrading for a number of decades before work starting on them a few years ago. It’s important to keep moving of the repair of our concrete resources. Successes on City Council I’ve been honored to serve as a Councilmember for the City of Belmont since first getting elected in 2022. We’ve had many successes as a City Council — including much better engagement with our residents and lots of progress on our roads and infrastructure. We are building in resilience for storm water and flooding with the recently completed Twin Pines Creek Restoration Project and are actively collaborating with neighboring cities on the bay’s effect on Belmont’s Island Park area. Our new Business License Tax structure is already attracting more businesses to Belmont, and our Recreation Programs have had increasingly accessible events for kids of all abilities. Our Police Department hired its first mental health clinician to assist officers in mental health calls, and we are almost finished with another affordable housing project on El Camino — one that also helps house formerly homeless folks. On a more individual note, each year, I’ve undertaken a different adventure here in Belmont! These include the First Friday Neighborhood Walks (started in 2023), the Belmont Restaurant Tour (2024), and the Day in the Life Series (2025) when, once per month, I spent a day with staff members from each city department to understand how they do their jobs. I love serving on county-wide committees, too! I spend time increasing sustainable commutes as the Board Chair of Commute.org. And, as Vice Chair of the Community Action Agency Board, I have my eye on how we are serving the most vulnerable of our population. https://www.xouhoabowen.com.title: Xouhoa Bowen for City Council
https://www.xouhoabowen.com.text: Xouhoa Bowen for City Council top of page MEET XOUHOA PRIORITIES ENDORSEMENTS ENDORSE DONATE BUILDING OPPORTUNITIES, DELIVERING RESULTS San Leandro, we've made meaningful progress, but there is still important work ahead. I will continue working to ensure San Leandro is a city where: Residents can afford their future. Neighborhoods are safe, clean, and connected. Small businesses and entrepreneurs can thrive. Infrastructure keeps pace with our community's needs. Housing is within reach for most people. Children, families, and seniors have the resources they need to succeed. Government is transparent, fiscally responsible, and accountable to the people that it serves. MEET XOUHOA I'm a mom of 3 wonderful kids, a refugee from Laos, a person with a disability, a nonprofit executive, a community organizer, a relentless optimist, and the first Asian woman to be elected to the San Leandro City Council. My parents brought my sister and me to America with hope, determination, and the belief that if they worked hard, their children would have opportunities they had never had. I learned that access to opportunity is what empowers a person to reach their fullest potential, and that every one of us can be the difference in making that a reality. ​ That belief shaped my life. ​ It led me to earn my BA in International affairs and psychology from Marquette University, a Master's in Business Administration from Norwich University, and executive certificates from the UC Berkeley Haas School of Business and Harvard Kennedy School of Public Policy. It inspired a career that includes serving in the Peace Corps , teaching citizenship classes in Milwaukee and English in Kyrgyzstan and South Korea, founding a nonprofit to empower women and their families , helping businesses grow, and strengthening communities through volunteerism and coalition building . When I first ran for City Council, it wasn't because I saw politics as a career. I ran because I knew I could make things better for real people in real ways. I ran because I wanted to help ensure that every family has the opportunity to build a good life and that decisions are made that reflect our diverse and rich community . Over the past four years, I've led with integrity , listened before making decisions , and focused on residents and what matters most to residents: safe neighborhoods, housing people can afford, a strong local economy, reliable infrastructure, quality public services, childcare and youth programming, and a City Hall that is transparent, fiscally responsible, and accountable. I know that different life experiences strengthen leadership. I'm proud to help ensure our government reflects and centers the people it serves while bringing people together around the values we share -- opportunity, belonging, forward progress, and a commitment to future generations. MY COUNCIL PRIORITIES Improving quality of life🩵 A great city is measured by how it feels to live here every day.​ What I've done... M ​ade quality of life a central focus of my work on the City Council. Advanced San Leandro's participation in the CalTrans Clean California initiative to improve neighborhood beautification, reduce litter, and create cleaner public spaces. Supported investments in parks, libraries, youth programs, summer camps, and public spaces that strengthen our community. Worked with residents to address neighborhood concerns like traffic, blight, illegal dumping, and improve city responsiveness. ​ ​ Why it matters: Clean, safe neighborhoods and robust city services strengthen community pride and increase community health and economic development. ​ Protecting our environment🍃 Protecting our environment means reducing waste, preparing for climate challenges, and building a healthier future for generations to come.​ What I've done... Advanced policies that reduce waste, strengthen climate resilience, and prepare San Leandro for the future. Introduced referrals to reduce single-use food packaging, encourage reuse, and explore home hardening strategies to help protect neighborhoods from wildfire risks. Supported efforts to improve neighborhood cleanliness, reduce litter, and expand sustainability initiatives. Advocated for thoughtful planning around emerging technologies, including evaluating the environmental impacts of AI data centers on our water, energy use, and infrastructure. Why it matters: Addressing climate change impacts helps to s afeguard public health, ensure long-term community resilience, and address environmental inequities. Growing a strong local economy💵 Supporting local businesses creates jobs, strengthens neighborhoods, and keeps our local economy growing.​ What I've done... Advocated for making economic development one of the City's top priorities . Helped integrate childcare into San Leandro's economic development strategy because families and employers both benefit from accessible childcare. Supported public safety and revitalization efforts that strengthen commercial corridors and attract investment. Worked with regional agencies to bring funding and economic opportunities to San Leandro. ​ Why it matters: A strong local economy means more opportunity, more jobs, and better city services.. Investing in infrastructure🏙️ Investing today saves money tomorrow and keeps our community safe.​ What I've done... Advanced the MacArthur Boulevard/Superior Avenue Roundabout to improve safety for everyone using the corridor. ​ Supported Safe Routes to School improvements and neighborhood traffic calming. Voted for investments in streets, sidewalks, transportation, and stormwater infrastructure. Advocated for securing transportation funding through my regional leadership. Why it matters: Reliable infrastructure improves safety, reduces future costs, and keeps San Leandro moving. Keeping our community safe🚨 Everyone deserves to feel safe in their neighborhood.​ What I've done... Supported investments in police, fire, and emergency preparedness. Backed traffic safety improvements to reduce collisions. Worked to improve neighborhood conditions by addressing blight and quality-of-life concerns. Supported balanced public safety strategies that combine prevention, enforcement, and community partnerships including the Alternative Response Unit and increased mental health services. Why it matters: Public safety is about protecting people while building stronger, healthier neighborhoods. Addressing housing and homelessness🏠 Every resident deserves the opportunity to live in a safe, stable home.​ What I've done... Supported stronger renter protections and rent stabilization to help prevent displacement along with guardrails to ensure efficacy and accountability. Voted to expand affordable housing opportunities and remove barriers to housing production. Supported investments in homelessness prevention, outreach, and San Leandro's first supportive housing center. Worked to balance neighborhood stability with responsible housing growth. Why it matters: Addressing housing affordability helps families stay in San Leandro while reducing homelessness over time. Governing with integrity📝 Government does best when it listens, plans for the future, and earns the public's trust.​ What I've done... Asked tough questions before major spending and development decisions. Championed transparency, fiscal responsibility, and meaningful community engaement. Called for thoughtful policies around AI data centers that ensure transparency and mitigations for adverse harm to our environment, infrastructure, water supply, neighborhoods, and quality of life before approval of projects. ​ Why it matters: Residents deserve leaders who make informed decisions - not rushed ones. ​ LEADERSHIP THAT DELIVERS BEYOND CITY HALL Effective leadership means making sure San Leandro has a voice wherever decisions affecting our community are made.In addition to serving as your Councilmember and Vice Mayor, I’ve earned the trust of my colleagues to represent San Leandro in leadership roles across Alameda County, the state, and the nation. These roles allow me to advocate for policies, partnerships, and funding that improve everyday life here at home. NATIONAL LEADERSHIP REGIONAL LEADERSHIP ENVIRONMENTAL LEADERSHIP As President of the Asian Pacific American Municipal Officials (APAMO) and a member of the Human Development Policy Committee with the National League of Cities, I work with local leaders from across the country to advance policies that strengthen families, expand economic opportunity, support immigrant communities, improve childcare, and ensure local governments have the tools they need to serve residents. As First Vice President of the East Bay Division of the League of California Cities, I collaborate with local leaders throughout the East Bay to advocate for legislation and funding that supports housing, transportation, infrastructure, public safety, and economic development for our region. ​ As Supervisor Tam’s representative on the Alameda County Transportation Commission, I advocate for safer streets, improved transit, and transportation investments that connect our community and improve mobility for everyone. As First Vice President of StopWaste, I help shape countywide policies that reduce food waste, improve recycling and composting programs, support climate resilience, and advance a more sustainable future—while helping residents and businesses save resources and reduce waste. WHY IT MATTERS Whether I’m working on transportation , environmental sustainability , housing , economic development , or local government policy , my focus is always the same: How do these decisions improve the everyday lives of the people who call San Leandro home? These leadership roles aren’t about titles. They’re about ensuring San Leandro has a respected voice, strong partnerships, and a seat at the table when important decisions are being made. https://adams4pittsburg.com.title: Re-elect Dionne Adams — Pittsburg City Council 2026
https://adams4pittsburg.com.text: Re-elect Dionne Adams — Pittsburg City Council 2026 Re-elect Dionne Adams · Pittsburg City Council 2026 Dionne Adams For Pittsburg City Council Home About Dionne Accomplishments Issues Get Involved Endorsements Contact Donate × Home About Dionne Accomplishments Issues Get Involved Endorsements Contact Donate Now Donate to our campaign Pittsburg City Council 2026 Re-elect Dionne Adams Pittsburg's Mayor and a fourth-generation resident, fighting to keep opportunity close to home. Together, we can build a Pittsburg where everyone is proud to work, live, and thrive. Donate Now Join the Movement Countdown to Election Day · November 3, 2026 -- Days -- Hours -- Minutes -- Seconds Current Mayor of Pittsburg Re-elect Dionne in November 2026 Stay updated Join the movement for a stronger Pittsburg. Sign Up About Dionne Deep roots. A clear mission. Serving as Mayor of Pittsburg since December 2025 From Pittsburg student to public servant My great-grandparents migrated to Pittsburg after World War II, joining many Black families who left the South seeking opportunity and a better life. They found it here, and four generations later, I am honored to serve the city that has given my family so much. I graduated from Pittsburg High School, went on to Diablo Valley College, and transferred to San Francisco State University, where I earned my Bachelor of Science in Business Administration with an emphasis in Marketing. I later completed my Master's in Public Policy from Golden Gate University. For over 20 years, I worked at PG&E in Oakland, leading belonging and diversity programming across diversity, equity and inclusion, supplier diversity, marketing, operations, and public policy. Why I came home What I remember most from growing up here is how my mother's job in town meant less commuting and more family time. People shouldn't have to leave Pittsburg to find good jobs or sit in traffic for hours. I returned home determined to make that reality for current and future generations. I started by joining city commissions and using my public policy background to contribute to our community. In 2022, I was elected to the City Council. In December 2025, I was unanimously selected by my fellow council members to serve as Mayor. Where I Serve Tri-Delta Transit Board Pittsburg Representative & Board Chair Bay Area Air District Contra Costa Mayors' Conference Rep; Vice Chair, Community Health, Equity & Justice Committee ABAG Board Member Community & Economic Dev. Council Subcommittee Infrastructure & Transportation Council Subcommittee Life Enrichment Council Subcommittee 4th Generation Pittsburg 70+ Years of Family Roots 20+ Years of Professional Leadership 2025 Unanimously Chosen Mayor Accomplishments Delivering results for Pittsburg. Since joining the Pittsburg City Council in 2022, Dionne Adams has worked to make major investments in Pittsburg’s infrastructure and quality of life, keep public safety a priority, strengthen the City’s financial footing, and expand opportunities for residents. $202M Invested in roads & infrastructure $11M Invested in Pittsburg parks $6M Invested in community facilities Fully Staffed Pittsburg Police Department Investing in Pittsburg’s Roads & Infrastructure Pittsburg is growing, and Dionne believes the City’s infrastructure has to grow with it. During her time on the Council, Pittsburg has invested $202 million in roads and infrastructure, supporting improvements to streets, utilities, public facilities, and other critical infrastructure throughout the city. During Dionne’s term, Pittsburg has also: Continued major road, water, utility, and public-facility improvements Advanced transportation planning focused on congestion and regional connectivity Continued investing in Pittsburg’s waterfront and public spaces, including the reopening of the renovated Central Harbor Park and Boat Launch in 2026 Parks, Recreation & Community Quality of life means having safe, welcoming places for families, young people, and neighbors to spend time together. During Dionne’s Council term, Pittsburg has invested $11 million in parks and $6 million in community facilities. The City’s strategic plans during her term have also expanded programming for residents, advanced Youth & Young Adult Services Master Plan objectives, and maintained youth and community enrichment as a City priority. That work includes: Continued investment in youth and recreation programs and the Marina Community Center Expanded community programming beyond traditional sports Work to create additional housing and supportive-service opportunities for transitional-age youth Keeping Public Safety a Priority Safe neighborhoods require sustained investment and a whole-community approach. Dionne has consistently identified public safety as one of her core priorities. During her Council term, Pittsburg has maintained a fully staffed Police Department and continued investing in the officers, equipment, partnerships, and community-based strategies necessary to keep neighborhoods safe. Dionne also believes public safety extends beyond policing. It means well-maintained streets, good lighting, safe crosswalks, community organizations, homelessness services, and neighborhoods designed so families feel secure. Making Tough Fiscal Decisions Strong communities need responsible finances. During Dionne’s time on the Council, Pittsburg has had to confront significant long-term budget pressures and make difficult decisions about City spending. Dionne has worked with her Council colleagues and City staff to strengthen Pittsburg’s financial position while protecting key investments in public safety, youth programs, roads, infrastructure, and essential City services, ensuring Pittsburg can continue delivering the services residents depend on for years to come. Expanding Opportunity Close to Home During Dionne’s time on the Council, Pittsburg has continued recruiting dozens of new businesses, supporting existing employers, and investing in the commercial corridors that serve residents. Dionne wants to build on that momentum over the next four years by bringing even more businesses and good-paying jobs to Pittsburg, supporting local entrepreneurs, and creating more opportunities for residents to work closer to home. Listening — and Acting — on Data Center Concerns When residents raised concerns in 2026 about Pittsburg’s approved data-center development and said they wanted more information and greater opportunities to participate, Dionne responded by pushing for additional public engagement. Following the June 15 Council meeting, the Mayor and City Council directed that data-center development return for additional Council discussion and public participation. The City subsequently held additional community engagement, including a dedicated City Council study session. In August, Pittsburg announced the creation of an Advisory Committee on Data Center Development to bring residents and stakeholders into the development of future City policy. Dionne’s position is that any major decision affecting Pittsburg neighborhoods should include clear information, accessible public engagement, and meaningful opportunities for residents to participate. My Vision for Pittsburg Four priorities that work together. Good jobs keep families in Pittsburg. Safe neighborhoods let kids thrive. Strong infrastructure attracts businesses. And when young people have real opportunity here, they stay. It's all connected. 01 Investing in the Next Generation Youth and Quality of Life I grew up in Pittsburg and had to leave to find opportunity. I came back so the next generation doesn't face that same choice. Every young person in this city deserves whole-child support: good schools, enrichment programs, safe spaces, mental health resources, and pathways to jobs and entrepreneurship right here at home. Expand after-school enrichment and youth development programs Prioritize funding for mental health and wellness support for young people Create workforce development pathways for youth not currently in school Expose kids to entrepreneurship and local job opportunities Support un-housed students at our junior college 02 Backbone of Our Community Good Jobs and Economic Development Pittsburg is a labor town, and our residents should not have to drive hours to find a good-paying job. I'm committed to bringing jobs closer to home, strengthening our business community, and making Pittsburg a place where people can work, spend, and stay. When families can afford to live here and find opportunity here, our whole community wins. Attract businesses and job centers that keep workers close to home Support small, diverse, and minority-owned businesses Build out Pittsburg's business district and commercial amenities Connect local businesses with the resources they need to grow Invest in workforce development through nonprofits and college partnerships 03 Keeping Pittsburg Safe Public Safety Everybody deserves to be safe, and public safety is a whole-community effort. I believe in a collaborative approach that brings together the Police Department, community organizations, and Public Works to address safety from every angle. We will use data to find gaps and patterns, ensure our approach is fair, and tackle the interconnected challenges facing our community. Invest in the Police Department while building strong community organization partnerships Improve street-level safety through Public Works: lighting, crosswalks, and infrastructure Address homelessness and the needs of unhoused residents as a public safety priority Ensure every neighborhood, family, and child in Pittsburg feels safe 04 Foundation for Growth Infrastructure and Transportation You cannot build a strong community on crumbling infrastructure. Pittsburg needs well-maintained roads, reliable utilities, modern facilities, and transit options that actually work for working families. As a Tri-Delta Transit Board representative, I'm already fighting for cleaner, more affordable, more connected transit. And as we grow toward a projected population of 100,000 by 2040, we need to plan and build accordingly. Expand affordable, clean, and reliable public transit routes and frequency Improve connections to BART and regional job centers Fix roads and address traffic pain points, including the San Marco corridor Invest in sustainable infrastructure that supports future growth Continue the water treatment plant upgrade to serve Pittsburg's growing population Pittsburg has always been very much a village — a close-knit, diverse community where people genuinely care for each other. https://www.votemjforec.com.text: Mary Ann "MJ" Jawili for City Council | Support Mary Ann "MJ" Jawili for El Cerrito City Council 0 Skip to Content Mary Ann "MJ" Jawili for City Council Why Vision Meet Volunteer Statement Endorsements Donate Open Menu Close Menu Mary Ann "MJ" Jawili for City Council Why Vision Meet Volunteer Statement Endorsements Donate Open Menu Close Menu Why Vision Meet Volunteer Statement Endorsements Donate I’m Mary Ann “MJ” Jawili I’m running for El Cerrito City Council. Donate 🙏 Donate 🙏 Volunteer ✋ Endorse 👍 View fullsize View fullsize View fullsize See more on Why I’m running I am running because El Cerrito deserves a leader who can bring its residents together, and I have a successful track record of listening with empathy, engaging people, and building community. I am running because I love El Cerrito, and I want to help it become a better, more inclusive, more sustainable, and thriving place to live. I am running because I think that public service is deeply rewarding, and I want to serve as an example to other people to show that they can do it, too. Contact me I love hearing from people. Contact me by phone or email. votemjforec@gmail.com (510) 467-0757 My vision Better connection, communication, and transparency I believe that trust and safety are built on connection, communication, and transparency. Politics in El Cerrito have become fraught and divisive over the past few years. Lack of transparency has caused a breakdown in trust between residents and city council. I will work to foster a city council environment that provides more opportunities to hear from residents, be responsive to input, and be transparent in the decision-making process. Better city communication I will prioritize increased communication and transparency between residents and city leadership by offering one-on-one office hours, commissioning surveys of residents, and meeting regularly with liaisons from various community groups. I also commit to communicating in plain language, across platforms and formats to meet residents’ diverse needs and preferences. Build safety through trust Everyone should feel safe calling for help—and confident that the right help will arrive. I believe public safety starts with strong relationships, prevention, dependable emergency response, and trust between residents and the people who serve them. I also believe safety and civil liberties belong together. That’s why I signed the Flock Out anti-surveillance pledge. Our community should not have to sacrifice their constitutional rights in the name of public safety. We should invest in approaches that work, measure the results, and be willing to change course when something isn’t working. We all want to feel more connected to our neighbors and our community. Community spaces are where we run into our neighbors and build new relationships. A connected community is a safe and thriving community. More community spaces Help local businesses thrive I want El Cerrito to be a place where local businesses can start, stay, and grow. That means filling empty storefronts, making it easier to reuse buildings for new purposes, and helping business owners navigate City Hall without unnecessary confusion or delay. I will work to build partnerships with local businesses such as cafes, shops, and gyms to facilitate the gathering of people in the community. A thriving local economy gives us great places to gather, creates opportunities for our neighbors, and helps pay for the public services we all depend on. Better and more accessible third spaces A strong community makes room for everyone. I want children to have safe places to learn, play, and grow. I want older residents to have places to gather, activities to enjoy, transportation they can depend on, and real human beings they can turn to for help. And I want people with disabilities to be able to participate fully in community life. This means protecting and improving our community centers, parks, trails, and improving the community programs that are currently offered. A multi-generational center A community thrives when residents across age and demographics are able to interact, connect, and build relationships. Our community needs both a senior center and a better library. But given El Cerrito’s limited resources, these two needs have been pitted against each other, resulting in tensions and divisions in our community. Our seniors deserve a dependable five-day-a-week gathering place to connect with each other and get help finding the services they need. Our kids deserve a place to learn and read that is safe. I will explore options for a multi-generational center that meets all of the needs of our diverse community. Accessibility isn't an extra feature. It's part of how we build a city where everyone belongs. Safe transportation and mobility We all want to be able to move through our community with ease. I aim to improve the ease and safety of transportation in El Cerrito so that it is easier for everyone to get where they want to go, connect with neighbors, and touch grass. Fix our streets and stop ripping them up twice Our streets belong to all of us, but a lot happens underneath them. Water, sewer, electricity, communications, and other infrastructure are maintained by different agencies and utilities. I want the City to coordinate those projects better so that we aren’t repaving a street only to have someone dig it up again. We should plan projects together, minimize closures and disruption, hold utilities accountable for restoring our streets properly, and make it easy for residents to know what work is happening and why. Improved and diverse transportation infrastructure I believe people should be able to easily get where they are going regardless of the mode of transportation they choose, whether that’s driving, biking, walking, or public transit. I support Complete Streets; frequent, public transit; accessible trails and sidewalks; reliable paratransit; and a functional network of transportation and mobility options for people to travel without driving themselves. We want our community to be able to respond to and withstand anything. While we can’t predict the future, we can prepare for it with smart budgeting and disaster preparedness planning now. Community resilience Spend our money wisely and explain where it goes El Cerrito has worked hard to recover from serious financial problems. We need to protect that progress. I’ll push for budgets that are understandable, realistic, and focused on the services residents actually experience — from roads and parks to emergency response and recreation. When we make difficult choices, residents deserve to know why. Good financial management isn’t just about balancing the books. It’s about making sure our money delivers real value for our community. Plan responsibly for pensions We made promises to the people who worked for our city, and we need to keep them. We also need to make sure those commitments don’t crowd out the services residents depend on today. I want El Cerrito to have a clear, long-term plan for its pension obligations, with understandable public reporting and realistic assumptions about the future. Residents, employees, and retirees should all be able to understand where we stand and what we’re doing about it. Prepare for the emergencies we know will come Wildfire. Earthquakes. Extreme heat. Flooding. Power outages. Preparedness isn’t just a plan sitting on a shelf. It means knowing how we will communicate, how people will evacuate, where they can get help, and how we will support neighbors who may need extra assistance. I want El Cerrito to practice these plans, find the gaps before an emergency happens, and work closely with neighboring cities, utilities, transit agencies, and Contra Costa County. How I’ll lead These policies are varied, but my approach to them is the same: Listen first. Be honest about what we know and what we don’t. Build on what works. Learn from what hasn’t. Measure whether we’re actually making things better. Most importantly, bring people together. Because I don't think the challenges facing El Cerrito belong to one neighborhood, one generation, or one political camp. They're ours to solve together. Email me at least 24 hours in advance so that I know to expect you. If this time doesn’t work for you, request an alternate time . We’ll try to find a better time. Candidate statement I've been a resident and homeowner in El Cerrito for 18 years, and I love this city. But in all the time I've lived here, I've never seen an election as polarized as our last primary. People feel they're not being listened to, and they've turned away from their city and their community as a result. Community is what I do. From hosting dinners with friends to serving as president of an 850-member cycling club, I work to bring people together. I do this professionally, too: For over a decade I've worked as a product leader in accessible technology, translating standards and people's needs into practical solutions that serve everyone, including people with disabilities and older adults. I've contributed to international standards and served on nonprofit boards, work that taught me how to listen, collaborate, and turn community input into tangible outcomes. Our city deserves leadership that listens first, cares deeply, and acts with integrity. As a city councillor I'll listen with empathy, especially to residents who feel unheard. I'll proactively meet residents where they are and communicate in plain language. I'll bring transparency to how decisions are made and how money is spent. I'll keep community at the center of policy because a city's greatness is measured by how well it serves its residents. El Cerrito doesn't need more division. https://votedonseta.com.title: Don Seta · Concord City Council District 3
https://votedonseta.com.text: Don Seta · Concord City Council District 3 Concord, California ✦ City Council · District 3 ✦ November 2026 Elect Don Seta Lt. Colonel, USAF (Ret.) For Concord City Council · District 3 ✦ Serve the Community. Safety Today. Green Future. Common-sense leadership for a stronger Concord. Donate Join the Campaign Read the Platform Contact Don Follow on Instagram Follow on Facebook ✦ A Word from Don Seta I come from a family of immigrants, who started with nothing. Just when they started to prosper, they were interned during WWII and had to start all over again. For them, hard work and a community that looked out for one another weren’t ideals — they were a way of life. I deeply understand the responsibility of community leaders to care for every resident in the community, with priority to those who need it the most. ✦ Get to Know Don Where I come from, being neighborly matters. I was born in Concord when my father farmed, and rows of fruit trees and vegetables outnumbered the neighbors. Our street was named after our neighbor, Mrs. Stimel. Walking home after school, we would stop at her house, and she fed us chicken soup. Concord is a place where neighbors look out for one another. Beyond Concord, I remember America cared for its neighbors and was respected by the entire world. My father, Concord, 1960 We are all immigrants , unless we descend from the Chupcan people — the original residents of Concord. My mother immigrated from Japan. She’s now 96 and a U.S. citizen, but like many in our community, she has fears. That’s why I serve on the Rapid Response team of the Concord Immigration Protection Network (CIPN). We work to ensure that anyone detained has their rights respected and their family notified. My mother, Concord, 1960 Old-School Values. My mother raised me with traditional principles — work hard, be humble, and never expect a handout. She believed in personal responsibility, strong families, and respecting the dignity of honest labor. Those values didn’t end with her; they’ve carried through with me, my children, and now my grandchildren. These values apply to Concord local government as well — to be accountable to taxpayers and avoid wasting their hard‑earned dollars. Don with grandson and his wife, Concord, 2026 About Me. Sometimes, I’m not the smartest person in the room — and when I’m not, I find them, earn their trust and turn them into allies or advisors. And I’m fearless. I’m not afraid to ask stupid questions, or challenge the emperor when he is naked. My courage comes from knowing I fight for those in need. A book I appreciate is Black Cat 2‑1 , where Bob Ford describes the fulfillment he found as an Army helicopter pilot serving his fellow soldiers with supplies and evacuations. His story reinforces a simple truth for me: real satisfaction comes from service. Don, Memorial Day, 2026 ✦ Credentials and Civic Leadership Roles Lt. Colonel, United States Air Force (Ret.) Doctorate in Business Administration, Alliant International University, San Diego Master of Science in Systems Management, University of Southern California, Los Angeles Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, University of California, Berkeley Director, Concord Ambassadors Director, Concord Historical Society Director, Concord Diablo Rotary Club Vice Chairman, Measure X Community Advisory Board Commissioner, American Legion Aerospace Commission of California Platform Priorities 01 📋 Serve the Community “The test of our progress is… whether we provide enough for those who have too little.” — Harry Truman I believe in responsible, fiscally disciplined city spending and in keeping District 3 fully informed about how and why decisions are made. I am equally committed to protecting our community and fostering an environment where opportunity is available to everyone. I intend to represent the needs of the constituents of District 3 and contribute to Concord's future. 02 🛡️ Safety Today The first duty of local government is to ensure the safety of its residents. District 3 families deserve timely emergency response and neighborhoods where people feel secure. I support Concord police, fire, and emergency services. These professionals put themselves at risk for our protection and deserve our support. Crisis preparedness can always improve, and I’m ready to champion that work. We can also strengthen pedestrian safety along our busiest streets — especially the Monument corridor — so people feel comfortable and confident moving through their own community. 03 🌳 Green Future Our parks are the living rooms of our neighborhoods — where children play, seniors walk, and families gather. Starting with Lake Ellis, regular maintenance is a must. I will fight to protect green space and upgrade park amenities in District 3. We also owe it to our children to leave the planet better than we found it. Green also signifies prosperity, starting with education. My Mexican Japanese American grandchildren have taught me an important lesson — Concord's strength lies in its brilliant, ambitious, multicultural youth. If District 3 schools are struggling, it's not the kids. Core Values Public Safety ✦ Honest Government ✦ Neighborhood Preservation ✦ Community First ✦ Get Involved District 3 wins when neighbors show up for each other. Tell us how you'd like to help, and we'll follow up. Full Name Email Phone Neighborhood How would you like to help? Canvassing / door-knocking Phone banking Yard signs Event support Office / admin help Other Availability Message (optional) Sign Up to Volunteer This opens your email app with your info filled in — just hit send. District 3 Deserves Principled Leadership. I was born in Concord, and I grew up watching my parents work to strengthen our community. I want to carry that tradition forward and help build a city government committed to safe neighborhoods & streets, and vibrant parks. And we need to balance the budget. Why I’m Running for City Council For 20 years, Piedmont is where my family has laid down deep roots. As an active working mom, I haven't just lived here—I've rolled up my sleeves and gotten involved. I’ve volunteered in our classrooms, coached our youth sports teams, and raised my family alongside yours. I know this community because I am a part of its daily rhythm. That same drive to be part of the community is what led me to step up as a leader for the League of Women Voters, to serve on the Piedmont Civil Service and Recreation Commissions, and now to run for City Council. I am also driven by a strong desire in public service, and for the past 27 years I have served as an attorney in the California Department of Justice working to protect the civil rights of all Californians. For the past three years I have been helping to shape our next generation of leaders by teaching law and public policy at the Goldman School of Public Policy at U.C. Berkeley. Keeping our city safe, our city amenities vibrant, and our infrastructure strong requires serious, proven leadership. I have spent years doing the groundwork and delivering results for our families on the local, statewide, and national level. I want to continue that work by taking a leadership role on the City Council and work with our dedicated City staff on the issues facing Piedmont including public safety, infrastructure, clean energy, and housing — all within the framework of an efficient and fiscally responsible agenda. It is my goal to be an accessible, responsive Councilmember who collaborates with residents and colleagues alike to make thoughtful, proactive decisions that put Piedmont first. I am honored to have this collaborative approach endorsed by our Mayor, Piedmont’s entire City Council and School Board, State Senator Jesse Arreguín, former Police Chief Jeremy Bowers, nine former Piedmont Mayors, and a broad coalition of community leaders and neighbors. Nancy is committed to responsibly meeting state housing mandates while ensuring Piedmont retains its hometown feel. https://www.drukerforwoodside.org.title: Daniel Druker for Woodside | Join the Movement—Support Beautiful Woodside
https://www.drukerforwoodside.org.text: Daniel Druker for Woodside | Join the Movement—Support Beautiful Woodside 0 Skip to Content Daniel Druker for Woodside Home About Dan Track Record Endorsements Contact Dan Open Menu Close Menu Daniel Druker for Woodside Home About Dan Track Record Endorsements Contact Dan Open Menu Close Menu Home About Dan Track Record Endorsements Contact Dan My Priorities for Woodside: Public safety & security Rural & equestrian heritage Community & recreation Responsive local government Managing state housing mandates Strategy & vision for the future I love Woodside - working on my tractors, hiking with my dogs, dancing at the Pioneer, meeting friends at Bucks, the Village Hub and the Little Store A nearly lifetime local, I have lived in Los Altos Hills, Palo Alto and Woodside since 1972. I earned an engineering degree from Stanford and an MBA from UCLA, and I am married with an amazing wife, five children and two dogs. After a great career as an operating executive for Silicon Valley startup technology companies, I retired in 2019 and in recent years I have been focused on public service in Woodside. Public safety, security and wildfire readiness are top of mind issues for Woodside district 3 residents In my service on the Town’s Circulation and Town Center Area Plan committees, I’ve helped to achieve major progress on public safety and transformation projects all over Woodside - from Four Corners to Woodside Elementary to Woodside Heights and Woodside High School. Learn more about my track record Woodside’s small town, rural character is what makes us different from other Bay Area Communities. I plan to work with Woodside’s equestrian community on a strategy to increase the number of horses that live and ride all across our town. I love Woodside’s rural and equestrian heritage Recreation and community building are my passion Improving the trails, pathways and outdoor recreational opportunities across beautiful Woodside is very important to me. In my service on the Town Center Area Plan committee, my focus has been on a long-term plan to evolve Woodside Town Center to be even more vibrant with public gathering spaces, improved retail offerings, and much more outdoor dining. Financial responsibility and responsive local government really matter Woodside is financially well managed. But our costs to provide public safety services are rising much faster than our revenues and we must get ahead of this. Our town is friendly and well run but we can always be easier to work with and more responsive to our residents and our local businesses. My top priority is long-term financial planning to make sure we can continue to provide excellent public safety services to Woodside residents over the coming decades. We must responsibly manage our compliance with state housing mandates As of July 1, Woodside had issued permits for 125 new housing units toward our goal of 328 new units under RHNA Cycle 6 (due by 2031) – so we are at 38% of the state’s target, which is far ahead of the Bay Area average of 14%. This great progress means that we hopefully will remain protected from oversized builder’s remedy projects which would be so out of character in Woodside. We should continue to try to make it faster, easier and less expensive for our property owners to build barns and ADUs and we need to remain best in class in the Bay Area in meeting our state-mandated housing targets. In terms of building more dense and lower income housing, I think we have a great opportunity to work with our major local employers – the Town of Woodside, Woodside Elementary, Woodside Fire, Menlo Country Club and the Family Farm for starters – to make it as easy and cost-effective as we can for each of these organizations to build attractive, appropriately scaled housing for our maintenance workers, teachers, firefighters, restaurant employees and other town staff so that these vital members of our community who work here can also afford to live in and enjoy Woodside if they wish to do so. We also need to starting thinking today about getting ahead of what will be coming in the next RHNA housing element cycle - cycle 7 - which starts in January 2031. About 70% of Woodside relies on septic systems for sewage management, and septic is currently incompatible with supporting state mandates for more dense housing. Our lack of sewer infrastructure is a serious bottleneck we are going to have to work with the county and the state to deal with. Woodside residents who live in districts 3 and 4 have also been vocal that they would like to see denser housing spread broadly around Woodside, and not exclusively concentrated in Woodside East of 280. A strategy and vision for the future There is so much more that I would love to do for Woodside… If elected, there are so many more safety and quality of life projects that I would like to see implemented in district 3 and across Woodside: I want to construct a pathway / bikeway / safe route to school along Woodside Road all the way from Alameda de las Pulgas past Woodside High School and Woodside Elementary School to Portola Road. This will require funding and cooperation from Caltrans, but I know we can do it! We have to improve safety for cyclists and pedestrians in the Four Corners area, extending for several miles north and south on Skyline and on the approaches to Skyline. Every year there are multiple pedestrian and cyclist injuries and fatalities in this area - it has to stop. I have heard strongly from you that outdoor dining is something you would like more of in Woodside. I would like to update our town’s regulations to provide our restaurants with more flexibility to offer outdoor dining and do this in a way that won’t create parking and traffic problems. I would like to complete our roadside trails network - we are just a few small inexpensive projects short of amazing walking loops for people and dogs (and in many places also horses) throughout beautiful Woodside district 3. We have made great progress on projects for student safety around Woodside Elementary such as the 15 MPH speed limit I worked so hard on to get passed over the last two years - but there is more work to do, especially with crosswalks, strategic traffic calming, parking, enforcement and improving the pick-up and drop-off processes at the school. We also need to improve student safety and create safe routes to school for the rest of the kids in Woodside that don’t attend Woodside Elm. This one is really hard - but I would like to figure out how to get bicycle Pelotons to more consistently obey traffic laws when they ride through Woodside. Enforcement is probably the only option, so this means finding budget. I want to partner with Portola Valley, Menlo Park and Atherton to push Caltrans to execute a major noise reduction project on 280. The pavement on 280 from the Stanford Linear Accelerator to Woodside Road is old, loud, broken concrete - and it is horribly loud 24×7. We need Caltrans to repave this section of 280 with noise-reducing asphalt and also look at making attractive landscaping changes to further reduce noise throughout Woodside. I want to see a comprehensive wildfire readiness and evacuation plan created and practiced across Woodside, plus I would like to see the Town work with our local neighborhoods to create cell phone, email and/or Whatsapp groups for local emergency communications as we have on Moore Road and in Woodside Hills and Woodside Heights. I would like to see Woodside pull together a long-term, prioritized capital funding plan to maintain, upgrade and replace our aging infrastructure, such as our bridges, drainage systems and crumbling mountain roads. I’d also like to explore the strategic expansion of our sewer infrastructure, which will likely become our most critical barrier to meeting future State housing element mandates. I love the public-private partnership model we created to fund the $2.5 million transformation of Woodside Road East of 280 into a parkway. I would like to explore a formal program to do more of this and build a list of candidate projects suitable for future public private partnerships - our residents are generous and there are many opportunities for projects that will improve safety and quality of life across beautiful Woodside. I would also like to be much more active in seeking county, state and federal grants to fund capital projects across Woodside. I am so excited about the long-term vision for transforming Woodside town center that we are working on in the Town Center Area Plan committee. I’d like Woodside town center to evolve to become even more vibrant, with an improved mix of consumer-focused retail, more outdoor dining, public gathering spaces and safe ways to get around town for people, dogs, bikes and horses. Big ideas, Real impact. In my volunteer roles, I’ve worked really hard to make Woodside an even more amazing place to live. I’ve learned so much about our beautiful town and what we can prioritize to make it even better. I’m so proud to have served alongside our dedicated, tenacious Woodside Town Council members, Town Volunteers, Town Employees, and our state and local agency partners to make impactful, tangible progress for our wonderful town. https://lauramelahn.com.title: Laura Melahn for Menlo Park City Council
https://lauramelahn.com.text: Laura Melahn for Menlo Park City Council About The Plan Endorsements Housing 10/22 Giving Day Donate New: 2026 Nobel Prize winner in Economics supports Laura for City Council → LAURA MELAHN for Menlo Park City Council · District 4 Housing solutions Downtown leadership Fiscal responsibility Love Menlo. Vote Laura. Donate Join 10/22 Giving Day A letter from Laura My name is Laura Melahn, and I am running to represent District 4 on Menlo Park’s City Council. I’m running because I love this place. I believe the good life is building something meaningful with other people in the place you share. But the way Menlo Park City Council is operating today is pushing residents out of civic engagement. I want to help make decisions that make sense to the people who have to live with them. My friends and neighbors saw my candidacy coming a mile away: when I galvanized our neighborhood to help make our streets safer for kids walking and biking, and built a citywide plan in the process; when I pulled our street together to save a 90-year-old heritage tree from developer destruction; and when I started a nonprofit dedicated to the simple goal of making our Downtown more inviting. I don’t want to be a City Councilmember in the abstract. I want to help Menlo Park do right by our residents, our businesses, and the physical place we are all so lucky to call home. Over the past several years, I’ve watched our City Council listen to everyone except the people who live here. That is what I will do differently. I’m running for the people of Menlo Park. I’m obviously not a career politician. If I were, I’d have better hair and smoother speeches. But I do know what it feels like to have my neighborhood’s concerns dismissed by our district representative. It’s terrible. So let’s change that. Love Menlo? Me too. Laura Melahn Laura at a Glance Co-founder, 501(c)(3) nonprofit Downtown Menlo Fund Chair, Menlo Park Finance & Audit Commission Creator, downtownmenlo.com & lovemenlo.com Author, Ollie’s First Day: An Oak Knoll Story Volunteer Coach, Menlo Park AYSO & Alpine Little League Board Member, The MAVEN Project Co-founder, Meadow Valley Partners Princeton University, Molecular Biology The Slow Streets Lady You might have some questions. Let’s answer them. Do you know how to do this job? Yes, I do, because I weirdly love it. I also like long distance running and once did a wall sit for 30 minutes, so there are some throughlines. There’s a short list of people who have attended more City Council meetings than I have these past few years and I’d wager no one who has watched more historical City Council YouTube content or read more agenda packets. The reason is, I believe in first-principles thinking, a prepared mind, and primary sources, so I’ve spent the time understanding how and why historical decisions have been made and what’s at stake for the future. I’m the Chair of Menlo Park’s Finance and Audit Commission and the Managing Partner of an investment firm, which turns out to be relevant for the coming years in Menlo Park, as we face a structural budget deficit that will require attention and fiscal responsibility. Who are you, “Laura Melahn”? Quick hits: I was born and raised in Hawaii, where I played endless amounts of soccer; studied molecular biology at Princeton, where I ran countless laps around the track; then did biochemistry research at Oxford University, where I again played lots of soccer. I arrived in the Bay Area 19 years ago and built a career at Google and GV, then put down roots with my husband and two boys in Menlo Park 6 years ago. In the community I coach soccer and baseball, convene weekly neighbor nights, wrote two books with Oak Knoll educators, and sit on the boards of both a healthcare access and downtown revitalization nonprofit. Professionally I’m a co-founder of Meadow Valley Partners, a healthcare investment fund and the CEO of Mauka Bio. What would you care about as a Menlo Park councilmember? I care about people, place, and process. People means listening to residents and valuing their quality of life. Place means protecting our city’s parks, heritage trees, open spaces, Downtown, and neighborhoods. Process means fiscal responsibility, logical decision making, effective execution, and accurate data. Our City government has a mission: “It is the mission of the City government to ensure that Menlo Park is a desirable and vibrant community in which to live and do business, and to respond to the values and priorities of the residents so as to provide for the community’s current and future needs.” It’s my goal to help the City live up to that stated mission. Read the full plan → Have you accomplished anything useful for the people of Menlo Park? I serve as the Chair of the Menlo Park Finance and Audit Commission, bringing analytical rigor to our fiscal commission. I co-founded the 501(c)(3) nonprofit Downtown Menlo Fund to support local businesses and bring investment downtown. This summer we launched Fourth Fridays bringing live music and good times to Santa Cruz Ave every month. I created downtownmenlo.com and the brand Love Menlo to drive placemaking and visibility for Downtown Menlo Park. I advocated for modernizing what types of businesses are allowed on Santa Cruz Ave through the Planning Commission process. Allowing more community-serving businesses is good for residents and for the vibrancy of Downtown. In particular, small-scale commercial recreation was not in staff’s draft plan. We advocated for it, got it in, and it’s why a family activity center can now open downtown! Making our neighborhood streets safer for kids, walkers, bikers, pets, and all was my entry point to engagement with the City. I’ve advocated for re-starting the paused Slow Streets Program to make our City more conducive to community building, social health, and safety. I’ve consistently encouraged that we try faster and less expensive pilots that are validated by other municipalities. A new Slow Streets Program was adopted in April 2026. I partnered with Oak Knoll educators to write Ollie’s First Day and Ollie Gets Ready , helping children who spent their earliest years in the pandemic make the transition to kindergarten. Custom versions of the book for Encinal and Laurel will launch this fall. What about housing in the downtown parking lots? It’s the question that has consumed this city for three years while producing zero building permits. It’s also worth being precise about the problem. Menlo Park is ahead of pace on market-rate homes, 59% of our target with five years to go, because the market builds those on its own. What we’re short of is very-low-income homes, the kind a preschool teacher or a home health aide can afford. That’s the dial to move, and it’s exactly the dial my plan moves. My housing plan works whether November’s initiative passes or fails, because most of Menlo Park’s affordable housing opportunity isn’t on the parking lots at all. It’s at Parkline, one block from downtown, and at the USGS campus, and it’s negotiable right now, before the election. I’ve published the Housing Element amendment that makes it official: teammenlopark.com/amendment . It’s even on Marsh Road, where the David D. Bohannon Organization has spent years asking the city for permission to build housing on its own land. Any downtown project gets the same test from me as everything else: does it pencil, and does it deliver very-low-income homes. As submitted, every one of the three current proposals gives something up: the very-low-income homes, the no-cost parking, or real construction wages. If we put everything from maintenance to economic development on hold behind one development idea, we’ll find ourselves trying to resuscitate Downtown as a dead patient. The best is yet to come for Downtown Menlo Park, and my plan doesn’t make anyone wait for it. Read the housing plan → Are you against housing downtown? No. Housing downtown is a good thing, and my plan shows it: Parkline will put hundreds of homes one block from downtown and equidistant to the train station. Any project on the plazas themselves gets the same test from me as every other site, does it pencil and does it deliver. What I’m against is confusing good intentions with a plan. The certified Housing Element promised 345 or more affordable homes downtown by 2027; it’s 2026 and there are zero permits. When someone says healthcare is broken, nobody thinks they’re anti-healthcare. Saying this plan is broken doesn’t make me anti-housing. It makes me the candidate who published a better one: the housing plan . Ask the people I’ve worked with Every endorsement here comes from someone who knows me and my work, from Menlo Park neighbors to former mayors to a former Governor and Secretary of the Navy. Endorsed by city leaders Ray Mueller San Mateo County Supervisor & Former Mayor of Menlo Park John Boyle Former Vice Mayor of Menlo Park Catherine Carlton Former Mayor of Menlo Park Paul Collacchi Former Mayor of Menlo Park Robert McNamara Former Mayor of Menlo Park Peter Ohtaki Former Mayor of Menlo Park Steve Schmidt Former Mayor of Menlo Park Mickie Winkler Former Mayor of Menlo Park Virginia Chang Kiraly President, Menlo Park Fire Protection District Board Rob Silano Menlo Park Fire Protection District Board Vice President “ I owe my career to California’s public schools, so I take seriously what a city does with the public’s money. A city is an economic system: a decision about one block of downtown affects the tax base and what the City can afford to do for everyone else. Laura Melahn understands that. She asks what a decision will actually do before she decides whether she is for it, which is rarer than it should be, and I am supporting her for City Council. Robert Hall 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics “ I only endorse people I actually know. I've worked with Laura and seen firsthand what she's capable of: she outworks everyone and she delivers results. Menlo Park would be fortunate to have her fighting for its future. Ray Mabus 75th United States Secretary of the Navy “ The choice is easy. Laura’s candidacy comes at a perfect time. The city needs a council member who can rise above divisiveness and find workable alternatives. Laura’s downtown revitalization project tells us how city problems can and should be solved. Clear thinking, enthusiasm and working together is Laura’s magic. Steve Schmidt Former Mayor of Menlo Park “ At HUD I saw a great many housing programs announced with confidence and never financed, usually because the promise came first and the economics came later, if at all. Laura Melahn starts by asking how a project will be paid for and whether the homes will actually get built. Menlo Park needs more affordable housing, and in my experience that is what it takes to get it built. I am supporting Laura for City Council. Susan Woodward Former Chief Economist, HUD “ Laura is uniquely qualified to manage the complex financial negotiations demanded by the constant stream of large scale development projects facing Menlo Park. Menlo Park has needed someone this bright with these skills for a very long time. Put her to work on the city council as fast as you can. Paul Collacchi Former Mayor of Menlo Park “ Laura was an amazing help as I prepared to open OFFLINE Pilates in Menlo Park. I knew the city from having worked here, but I had never navigated it as a business owner, and finding the right space was proving harder than I expected. Laura told me about the changes happening downtown and how they could benefit a business like mine. We grabbed coffee, talked about the city, and walked the streets together as she showed me available storefronts. She told me what she wants to do to make Menlo Park even better, and she connected me with city officials who were wonderful to work with. That’s the kind of person Menlo Park needs on City Council! Makini Mask Founder, OFFLINE Pilates Makini Mask OFFLINE Pilates “ Clear headed and intelligent. Laura understands the needs of the Downtown business community. Most important, she is grounded in fiscal responsibility and the necessary management metrics for creating government efficiencies. Draeger's Markets strongly endorses her candidacy. Richard Draeger Draeger's Super Markets, Inc. “ Family and kid focus. Smart as a whip. Loves Menlo and will help transform the City for the future. Ben Eiref Former Planning Commission Chair “ Laura is the kind of neighbor who gets things done for Menlo Park. She partners with our teachers, builds for our community, and shows up when it counts. She’s who we need on Council. https://www.suenoack.com.title: Sue Noack for PH City Council
https://www.suenoack.com.text: Sue Noack for PH City Council Toggle navigation Home Get to Know Sue Action Endorsements Donate Contact Sue Admin × Thanks! It has been four months since my swearing in at City Council. I want to thank all of you that supported me through the campaign process and through my first months as a City Councilmember. This message is late but is still as heartfelt. The experience to date has been terrific. I have been to the League of Cities conference for new city councilmembers and to a second for planning commissioners. Both were great sources of information and gave me the ability to meet representatives from many neighboring cities. The City Council meetings to date have included a variety of topics and I feel I have already been able to contribute. I have been assigned to several committees/boards and have attended meetings at CCCTA, Transpac, the Library Task Force, and the Economic Development committee. I look forward to many future meetings and increasing my participation. One of the things I loved about the campaign was getting to meet so many great people in Pleasant Hill. I want to continue doing that throughout my term. Please stop me and say hi if you see me at the grocery store, walking my dog or attending one of our great City events. I look forward to serving you all. Thanks again. Close I have proudly served the City of Pleasant Hill for twelve years including three years as Mayor. Some of my proudest accomplishments and activities are: Measure K was passed. This sales tax measure allowed our city to tackle many infrastructure projects such as road repaving and storm drain improvements. It also allowed us to build the new city library. Pleasant Hill Library. Our state-of-the-art library opened in 2022. I was part of the subcommittee since its inception and remain on it today for any city related decisions. This library reflects our welcoming city and encourages imagination, activity, learning and community. It is a Net Zero library, producing as much power as it will use. Addressed issues related to Covid. Measures were taken to help our businesses adapt to the various phases of Covid as well as ensuring city services could be delivered. Supported the Pleasant Hill Perks program along with grant process for businesses to improve their online presence. To reinforce Pleasant Hill as an inclusionary city , a resolution was passed to set a high standard for how we treat people regardless of race, religion, gender or orientation. The Diversity subcommittee of the Civic Action Commission and its successor the Diversity Commission will continue our focus in this area. Pleasant Hill 2040. I sit on the General Plan Advisory Committee working on developing our general plan for the next 20 years. This process has also included our new Housing Element where we have had to address the challenging Regional Housing Needs Allocation. This process continues and we will continue to strive to improve public involvement. Regional Involvement. I sit on a number of boards representing Pleasant Hill and Central Costa County including; County Connection Board, Transpac (regional transportation planning board), CCTA (Contra Costa Transportation Authority board, and the Innovate 680 policy advisory committee. I also represent the 19 cities of Contra Costa on the Metropolitan Transportation Commission for which I am currently serving my second year as Chair. Our future is not without challenges. My background in finance allows me to play a vital role on City Council and our Budget Committee. The City's unfunded pension liability will create some financial challenges and will require a watchful eye and the development of ways to address it. Through our Measure K funds and working with regional agencies, we need to continue to work on traffic issues and opportunities for alternate forms of transportation. We need to work with the school district and DVC as local traffic can be significantly impacted by school-related transportation. You have honored me with your past support, and I hope you will consider supporting me again in November. Sue Noack
